payload.title: [native-swift-5] FrickStore/FrickCallSession do not drop rows deleted while disconnected — stale rows persist af...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING native-swift-5 (medium/correctness, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: packages/swift/Sources/FrickSwift/FrickStore.swift
LINES: 160-215

WHAT: On reconnect the socket replays `activeSubscriptions` and the server resends a snapshot, surfaced as `.objectsDelta` (handleSnapshot, FrickSyncSocket.swift:1368-1379). `FrickStore.apply(records:)` only inserts/merges by id and never clears the cache, and `apply(removals:)` only acts on explicit `.objectsRemoved` events. A row deleted server-side WHILE the client was disconnected is simply absent from the reconnect snapshot — no removal event is generated for it — so it lingers in `byId`/`items` indefinitely. `FrickCallSession` (roomsById/participantsById) and the snapshot-as-delta path have the same gap.

IMPACT: After an offline window during which a record was deleted (or access revoked), the deleted row stays visible/usable in the UI until the store is `reset()` or the app restarts. Shows stale (potentially access-revoked) data; can mislead the user and, for shared records, surface content the user should no longer see.

SUGGESTED FIX: Distinguish a fresh snapshot from an incremental delta (the socket already has the snapshot vs delta frame kinds) and have stores reconcile to the snapshot set — drop cached ids not present in the snapshot — rather than pure-merge.
